audit.why: Emerald+ 51.32% over 7794 games — the largest sample in this slice. Darius owns the early lane; Nautilus's value is tank scaling and Depth Charge roams, which the existing early/mid/late split already states.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 chart entry carried a leaked LaTeX formula (R = d + a \times Stacks) and never named Depth Charge, which is the only thing that changes for Nautilus at 6.
audit.why: Depth Charge is 120/100/80s — the same cooldown as your own ultimate at every rank — and it is a chasing projectile that knocks up and stuns. The stage should say who spends first.
audit.corrected: Level 6 why now keeps the true-damage point and states the 120s-to-120s ultimate trade.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.early said Nautilus 'shields with E' and told you to pull 'when his E shield is down'. Riptide (E) is a three-wave slow with no shield; the shield is Titan's Wrath (W).
audit.why: Riot's text: Riptide 'creates three exploding waves around himself. Each explosion damages and slows enemies.' Titan's Wrath 'gains a temporary Shield. While it persists, his Attacks deal damage over time to his target.' Waiting on the wrong ability means waiting on a 5-7s cooldown instead of the 12s one that actually decides the trade.
audit.corrected: Shield attributed to Titan's Wrath with its 12s flat cooldown as the step-up cue; Riptide named as the slow. Staggering Blow's root-on-first-attack written into the don'ts as the reason run-downs fail.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cooldown block had no numbers — 'His only engage. Dodge it.' and 'Long early cooldown'.
audit.why: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 at 1150 range, Titan's Wrath 12s flat, Riptide 7s at rank 1, Apprehend 26s at rank 1. The 14s hook window is the whole punish.
audit.corrected: Cooldown block and the first do now carry the real numbers.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.wave and report[4].t had the cooldowns and trading sections spliced into the middle of the wave text, and breakdown.trading contained a stray page-header fragment.
audit.why: Visible corruption, and it displaced the one thing that matters about waves here: Dredge Line pulls him to terrain, so where in the lane you fight decides whether he can leave.
audit.corrected: All three rewritten in-band; wave text now says to fight on the open side of the lane away from walls.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two don'ts and one do had bodies copy-pasted from the trading block that did not match their headings ('Eat his passive root chain', 'Extend into his W shield', 'Pull when his E is down').
audit.why: Each heading names a mechanic the body never explained, and the do's heading pointed at the wrong ability slot.
audit.corrected: Bodies replaced with Staggering Blow's root and Titan's Wrath's 12s shield window; the do's heading corrected from E to W.

edits.before: Naut hooks (Q), roots with passive autos, and shields with E. Dodge his Q, avoid the chain-CC, and pull + bleed when his E shield is down. No real kill threat. Don't chase past the wave into Dredge Line (Hook).
edits.after: Naut hooks with Dredge Line (14s at rank 1), roots with Staggering Blow, and shields with Titan's Wrath (12s) — Riptide only damages and slows. Sidestep the anchor, then pull and bleed while the shield is down.

edits.before: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage R = d + a \times Stacks, bypassing defensive items completely. The execute resets on takedowns — all-in windows are now real kill windows.
edits.after: Noxian Guillotine is true damage scaled by Hemorrhage stacks, so his shield and armour do nothing. Depth Charge is 120s, the same as yours — whoever spends it first loses the next fight.

edits.before: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): matchup-defining — His only engage. Dodge it. Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane.
edits.after: - Nautilus Dredge Line (Hook): 14s at rank 1 from 1150 range — his only engage and his only escape. Sidestep it and you have fourteen seconds. Titan's Wrath: 12s flat, so the shield is the real trade timer. Darius E (Apprehend): 26s at rank 1 — never throw it predictably; hold it to yank him off a wall or out of his retreat. Darius Ghost: keep it for the run-down through Riptide's slow, not the walk-up.

edits.before: His only engage. Dodge it. Bait it, count it, then go.
edits.after: Dredge Line is 14s at rank 1 — bait it, count it, then go.

edits.before: Pull when his E is down
edits.after: Pull when his W shield is down

edits.before: Pull Nautilus as he steps to last-hit, W slow, land the Q outer ring, weave two autos, and walk away at 3-4 stacks with the heal banked.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath is 12s flat — step up as it drops, pull, W-slow, land the outer blade, and bank 3-4 stacks before it returns.

edits.before: Your committal tool is the lane — burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Staggering Blow roots on his first attack on you — that root, not his damage, breaks your run-down.

edits.before: Whiffing Apprehend and then fighting anyway — without the pull you have no engage, and chasing through a wave bleeds you dry.
edits.after: Titan's Wrath makes his autos burn you while it holds; extend into a fresh shield and you trade his 12s cooldown for your 26s E.

edits.before: Best wave: your highest priority is maintaining a slow-building freeze locked directly outside your turret range. This completely denies them the safety of a short lane, leaves them highly exposed to devastating jungle collapses, and grants you an incredibly long runway to activate Ghost and run them down the lane the exact millisecond they waste an essential safety mechanism. Key Mechanical Cooldowns Darius E (Apprehend): Long early cooldown. Never throw this out predictably; save it explicitly to interrupt their dash trajectories mid-flight or catch their retreat paths. Darius Ghost: Your primary lethal enabler. Keep this tool ready to completely blow through ranged poke or instant slows across the lane. How Darius Wins Trades Look for them to walk forward to secure a critical minion last hit. Step up instantly, land an auto-attack directly into a fast Crippling Strike (W) reset, and use the heavy slow to step back out of their counter-abilities. If they panic and waste their primary mobility or crowd control tool, activate Ghost immediately, pull them back with Apprehend, and stack your passive to full for an easy execution loop. • • Worst wave: shoved to his tower with Apprehend and Ghost down. Crash timing: only crash to reset, take plates, or set up a dive — never shove on autopilot.
edits.after: Best wave: your highest priority is maintaining a slow-building freeze locked directly outside your turret range. This completely denies them the safety of a short lane, leaves them highly exposed to devastating jungle collapses, and grants you an incredibly long runway to activate Ghost and run them down the lane the exact millisecond they waste an essential safety mechanism. Nautilus is the rare top laner who does not mind a shoved lane, because Dredge Line pulls him to terrain and out of a gank, so the freeze has to be tight enough that he is standing in the open when you step up rather than hugging a wall. Hold the wave two or three casters outside your turret, last-hit late, and take the fight on the open side of the lane where his anchor has nothing to grab. When he shoves to roam with Depth Charge, do not chase — crash the wave back, take the plate, and ping the lane he is walking to. Level 1 he will try to shove for the anchor-to-terrain gank angle, so match the push only far enough to keep the wave off your plates and never past the river bush without vision. Worst wave: shoved to his tower with Apprehend and Ghost down. Crash timing: only crash to reset, take plates, or set up a dive — never shove on autopilot.

edits.after: Good trade: Look for them to walk forward to secure a critical minion last hit. Step up instantly, land an auto-attack directly into a fast Crippling Strike (W) reset, and use the heavy slow to step back out of their counter-abilities. Titan's Wrath is 12s flat, so time the step-up to the moment the shield drops rather than to your own cooldowns. If they panic and waste their anchor or their shield, activate Ghost immediately, pull them back with Apprehend, and stack your passive to full for an easy execution loop. Bad trade: Whiffing Apprehend and then fighting anyway — without the pull you have no engage, and chasing through a wave bleeds you dry.
